posts.hook: Getting paid faster is the cheapest raise you'll ever give yourself.
posts.why: Every day an invoice sits unpaid, your money is funding someone else's business. Most late payments aren't bad customers. They're friction.
steps: Send the invoice the same day the job is done, not at the end of the week.
Put a pay now link for card or bank transfer right on the invoice.
Put the due date in bold at the top, and send a friendly reminder the day after it passes.

posts.hook: What to say when a customer tells you “that's too expensive.”
posts.why: Jumping straight to a discount teaches customers to haggle. Most of the time, “too expensive” really means “I don't see why it's worth it yet.”
steps: Don't argue. Ask “Compared to what?” and really listen to the answer.
Explain what they get, not what you do. The result, the warranty, the cleanup, the peace of mind.
If budget is truly the problem, offer a smaller option instead of a lower price for the same work.
posts.take: Cut the scope, never your worth.

captions.facebook:

posts.hook: The 2 minute rule that keeps your to do list from eating you alive.
posts.why: If a task takes less than 2 minutes, doing it now is faster than writing it down, remembering it, and coming back later. It comes from David Allen's Getting Things Done.
steps: Today, every time something lands that takes under 2 minutes, do it right then.
Anything longer goes on one list. Not in your head, not on 5 sticky notes.
Block 30 minutes tomorrow morning for the hardest thing on that list, before you open your email.
posts.take: Small stuff done now. Big stuff done first. That's the whole system.
